scenario_name: Sustained classification at one estimated H100 ModernBERT-large equivalent

gpu_assumption.throughput_derivation: 350,000 H100 tokens/s observed for ModernBERT-base multiplied by the official RTX 4090 short-variable large/base throughput ratio, 52.9/108.7
gpu_assumption.throughput_status: Proxy estimate, not a benchmark of MoritzLaurer/ModernBERT-large-zeroshot-v2.0 on the target serving stack
gpu_assumption.utilization_assumption: Near 100%; continuous fractional GPU-equivalents represent a sufficiently large, fully utilized fleet
excluded: CPU and RAM charges beyond the assumed H100 hourly price
storage, network egress, orchestration, redundancy, and engineering
cold starts and unused reserved capacity

modernbert_zero_shot.formula: sum_i tokenize(state, question_i), approximately N * state + sum(question_i) + pair special tokens

modernbert_trained_heads.formula: tokenize(state) once, then 27 fixed logistic heads; question text is not an inference input
modernbert_trained_heads.question_flexibility: Fixed learned taxonomy; a new question requires a new or retrained head

jev_noul.formula: Observed billing is consistent with state + N * question + fixed overhead

jev_choice.formula: Observed billing is consistent with state + question and criteria tokens + fixed overhead
jev_choice.question_flexibility: Arbitrary typed questions and options at inference

interpretation: The trained ModernBERT result is extremely inexpensive because its 27 questions are fixed in learned heads; it is not an arbitrary-question system.
Zero-shot ModernBERT preserves arbitrary hypotheses but repeats the state inside every NLI pair, creating a measured 28.67x token-compute amplification for 27 questions.
JEV preserves arbitrary typed questions while billing as shared state plus incremental question tokens, but billing behavior does not prove the internal compute graph.
The JEV API capacity required to sustain this hypothetical load was not tested; its cost is linearly extrapolated from published per-token pricing.
